sentences.text:
By the impugned award, the learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 4,83,000/- in
favour of appellants/claimants on account of death of deceased Kamta Prasad Tiwari, in an
unfortunate accident that took place on 07.05.2015.

As per the pleading of the claim application
deceased was going to attend a marriage function from village Pendra to Bilaspur sitting in the
vehicle
Scorpio bearing registration No. Cg 12-Ak 4196 (for short "the offending vehicle")

. The
offending vehicle was driven rashly and negligently by the driver and caused the accident in which
the deceased sustained severe injuries and was brought to Cims Hospital Bilaspur, where he was
declared dead.

It was pleaded that the deceased was working as Manager in Pitamber Traders and
was earning Rs. 18,000/- per month, therefore, the appellants/claimants claimed Rs. 52,00,000/-
as compensation.

The respondent No.1/owner filed the written statement and denied the averments
of the claim application.

and has specifically pleaded that the offending vehicle was insured with
respondent No.2/Insurance Company therefore the liability to pay the compensation is upon the
/respondent
No.2 /
Insurance Company

. 
3. Respondent No.2/Insurance Company also filed its written statement and denied the averments
of the claim application.

It has admitted the Insurance policy and pleaded that more persons than
the sitting capacity of the offending vehicle were seated and therefore there is violation of the terms
and conditions of the Insurance policy and prayed for exoneration from paying the compensation.
4. On the basis of the above broad pleadings, the learned Tribunal has framed as many as five issues.

Issue with regard to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, violation of the
Insurance Policy and Income of the deceased was decided in favour of the Neutral Citation
2023:Cghc:23219 appellants/claimants however instead of Rs. 18,000/- per month, Rs. 3,000/-
per month income has been assessed.

In Issue no. 4 & 5, relief and cost, the compensation to the
tune of Rs. 4,83,000/- was awarded.

5. Shri Chaturvedi, learned counsel for the appellants/claimants vehemently argued that from the
evidence available on record, the monthly income of the deceased was proved as Rs. 18,000/- per
month and the learned Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of Rs. 3,000/- per
month.

He further submits that the future prospect was not awarded and the amount of
compensation under the legally admissible heads is also on the lower side and therefore the amount
of compensation be suitably enhanced.

6. Ms. Chitra Shrivastava, learned counsel for the respondent No.2/ Insurance Company submits
that the learned Tribunal has rightly rejected the monthly income of the deceased to Rs. 18,000/-
per month as from the statement of Manish Kumar Shukla (Aw-2), it is very categorically
established on record that the deceased was not earning such income as no documents with regard
to the identity of the firm in which the deceased was said to be working, is brought on record except
a register has been brought which has been rightly disbelieved by the learned Tribunal.

7. Heard counsel for the parties and considered the rival subm

issions.
8. From the evidence of Manish Kumar Shukla (AW-2) and the findings recorded by the Tribunal rejecting the monthly income of the deceased as Rs. 18,000/- does not appear to be perverse and in a detailed cross- examination it has been admitted by AW-2 that the payment of Rs. 18,000/- was not mentioned in the income tax return, no document with regard to the firm has also been filed and the amount was being paid to him in cash.
And no such receipt is filed.
AW-2 has admitted that the deceased was his Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:23219 brother-in-law.
Register (Ex.P-12) does not contain his signature and seal of Pitamber Traders.
Considering the entire evidence, the learned Tribunal has rightly rejected the monthly income of deceased to Rs. 18,000/-.
However the assessment of the income of the deceased to Rs. 3,000/- is absolutely on the lower side and requires proper enhancement.

The date of incident is 07.05.2015 on the basis of oral evidence and the nature of job and the minimum wages prevailing at that point of time, this Court can safely infer the monthly income of the deceased to Rs. 6,500/- and 25% future prospect is also added in view of the judgment of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.,
(2017) 16 SCC 680.

9. Since the Tribunal has already awarded Rs. 4,83,000/-, after deducting the same from the above amount, the claimants are held entitled for additional compensation of Rs. 7,70,750/-.

10. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part and the award impugned is modified to the extent that the claimants/appellants shall be entitled to a total amount of compensation of Rs. 7,70,750/-/-
with a payment of interest on the enhanced amount of compensation @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual payment.
11. The respondent No.2/Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced amount of compensation within 60 days.
After deposit, Rs. 50,000/- (each) shall be disbursed to appellant No. 2 to 5 through bank transaction/account payee cheque.
Rs. 5,00,000/- shall be invested as fixed deposit in a Nationalized Bank for a period of 2 years in the name of appellant No.1.
Remaining amount shall be disbursed to appellant No.1 through Bank transaction/account payee cheque.
12. No order as to costs.
